chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام, “When does the time of Zuhr enter?” He said, “When the sun declines.” I said, “When does its time go out?” He said, “After four feet have passed from its decline. Indeed, the beginning of the time of Zuhr is narrow.”

I said, “Then when does the time of Asr enter?” He said, “Indeed, the end of the time of Zuhr is the beginning of the time of Asr.” I said, “Then when does the time of Asr go out?” He said, “The time of Asr is until the sun sets, and that is due to an excuse; otherwise it is neglect.”

So I said to him, “If a man were to pray Zuhr after four feet have passed from the sun’s decline, would he, in your view, be one who has not properly performed it?” He said, “If he did that deliberately in order to oppose the sunnah and the appointed time, it would not be accepted from him—just as if a man were to delay Asr until near sunset deliberately, without an excuse, it would not be accepted from him. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم appointed times for the obligatory prayers and set limits for them in a sunnah for the people. So whoever turns away from a binding sunnah among his sunnahs is like one who turns away from the obligations of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ: a measured span used here to indicate a prayer-time boundary after zawal
key_terms.السُّنَّةَ: the binding Prophetic practice regarding prayer timings
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun’s decline from the zenith, marking the start of Zuhr
key_terms.عِلَّةٍ: a valid excuse or reason affecting delay
key_terms.فَرَائِضِ اللَّهِ: the obligations imposed by Allah, Mighty and Majestic
key_terms.وَقْتُ الظُّهْرِ: the time period مقرر for the Zuhr prayer
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْعَصْرِ: the time period مقرر for the Asr prayer

ai.seo_question: When do the times of Zuhr and Asr begin and end according to Imam Musa al-Kazim عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the times of Zuhr and Asr prayer, explaining that Zuhr begins at the sun’s decline and that Asr begins at the end of Zuhr’s specified preferred time. It also stresses that intentionally opposing the prescribed sunnah timing of the obligatory prayers without excuse renders the act unacceptable, highlighting the binding force of the Prophetic sunnah (prophetic tradition).
